title: Secretary of State of Wisconsin

context.text: The seat is open: appointed Secretary of State Sarah Godlewski is running for lieutenant governor, the first election in more than 40 years without an incumbent seeking the office.

Wisconsin's Secretary of State does not administer elections, which are run by the bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission; the office keeps the state seal, validates the state's presidential electoral certificate, and sits on the Board of Commissioners of Public Lands.

candidates.name: JoCasta Zamarripa
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 11 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Quoted in her campaign announcement: "I’m running for Secretary of State to be a strong voice for all Wisconsinites"

Using the office's platform and its seat on the Board of Commissioners of Public Lands, which helps manage more than $1.3 billion in trust funds supporting school libraries, to advocate on cost of living, child care, housing and school funding.
Keeping election authority with the Wisconsin Elections Commission rather than moving it to the Secretary of State, as reported by Ballotpedia News.

candidates.name: Jay Schroeder
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11 Republican primary with about 47% of the vote in election-night counts, ahead of the party-endorsed candidate.

priorities.text: Moving the role of chief election official from the Wisconsin Elections Commission to the Secretary of State: "Moving the role of Chief Election Official back to the Secretary of State."
Records transparency and removing what his site calls the commission's "bureaucratic shield."

candidates.name: Pete Karas
candidates.ballotNote: Wisconsin Green Party nominee; no contested primary.

priorities.text: Electing a candidate outside the two major parties: "Break the Two-Party Grip. Vote for Real Change."

candidates.researchNotes: Only a campaign homepage and a voter-guide summary were found; no issue positions beyond the two-party-system message.

researchNotes: Slate: Dane County Clerk's certified 'What's on the Ballot' list for Nov. 3, 2026 shows Jay Schroeder (REP), JoCasta Zamarripa (DEM) and Pete Karas (GRN) for Secretary of State, matching The Green Papers; the Wisconsin Elections Commission files sit behind a bot check and were not bypassed. The Green Papers also shows a Working Families line for Zamarripa that the Dane County ballot list does not print, so only the Democratic line is recorded. Zamarripa's own record as an alderperson and legislator was not itemized because no official roll-call pages were reviewed. No candidate's own words address documentary proof of citizenship; the race centers on who administers elections, which the Secretary of State does not currently do.
